2. The case was set out in motion by Halima Khatun who lodged First Information Report with the Bagerhat Police Station, but she could not be examined as a witness in the trial court as she died before the trial commenced. Her deposition recorded in the committing court has, however, been admitted as additional evidence under Section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by this Court on the prayer of the learned Advocate for the state without any objection from the side of the learned advocate for the appellants. 

 5. The prosecution case as given by P.W.1 may be taken up first and then the evidence of other witnesses will be discussed. P.W. 1 Sheik Atiar Rahman is the son of the deceased Akbor Sheik. He accompanied his father deceased Akbar Sheik at the time when the occurrence took place. He said that prior to the occurrence in question there had been a quarrel in between accused persons who are the members of the Kazi family and his father over cutting sugarcane from the lands belonging to his father by the boys of the Kazi family and in pursuance thereof the accused persons were hatching a conspiracy to kill his father. His father did not pay heed to such affairs though he (P.W. 1) informed him of the conspiracy in due time. On the date of occurrence on 11.10.78 at about 6/7 P.M. his father started for the heel with a net to catch fish there and he himself was getting ready to join his father after having his meal, all on a sudden he heard a hue and cry from the side of the bank of the heel where the boat was anchored and at once he ran towards that place and found that accused Mobin Sheik, Amjad Sheik, Razzaque Kazi, Aftab Kazi, Babul Kazi, Khokon Kazi and Nazim Kazi were assaulting his father, while he raised alarm Babul Kazi and Nazim Kazi caught hold of his neck and accused Khokon Kazi, Amzad Sheik caught hold of his hands. The accused persons then took the victim Akbar Sheik to the house of Mannan Kazi and assulted him inhumanly. Thereafter, the accused persons dragged the victim near the shop of Shahid Kazi and continued to assault him there also. The witness was also dragged there by the accused persons. In the meantime, accused Mannan Kazi returned from Bagerhat and ordered for finishing the victim Akbar Sheik on which the accused Khokon Kazi brought a Sabol from the Shop of Shahid Kazi, accused Razzaque and Aftab Kazi caused fracture and damage to the legs of the victim by Sabol blows. Accused Kanai Kazi and Khokon Kazi damaged the hands and the eye of the victim was extracted. The accused persons carried the victim to the house of local Chairman in a gunny bag and fled away after leaving him there. The Chairman and his cider brother Ahiya came out of the house and made arrangement for sending the victim to Bagerhat Hospital by a rickshaw. Mother and step-mother of the witness came there and they also started for Hospital by a separate rickshaw. He denied the defence suggestion that he was aware that his lather was caught while committing theft in the house of Dabiruddin. He started for the place where the boat was and there were houses of Jalal Sheik, Mohiuddin Sheik, Momtaz Sheik and Abdul Wahab. The houses of Kalam Sheik, shop of Shahid Kazi and houses of Ramjan and Jamir were also close to the place where his father was assaulted. The witness admitted that he was in hazat being accused in the case of attempt to murder of one Mofi Sheik. 

 7. Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, argued that the learned trial Court ignored the inconsistencies between the statements made in the F.I.R. and the deposition of the above mentioned two witnesses and illegally admitted the F.I.R. as substantive evidence and relied on the same for the purpose of corroborating the evidence of the prosecution witnesses and thereby committed error of law in convicting the appellants. The learned Advocate has further submitted that the evidence of the P.Ws. shows complete departure from the statement made in the in material particulars and this has rendered the prosecution case not only weak but also unreliable. 

 8. Mr. S.B. Barua, the learned Advocate for the State, by way of supporting the judgment of the trial court while admitting that the F.I.R. is not the substantive evidence contends that F.I.R. being the initial statements of the prosecution is an important piece of document and it can be used for the purpose of corroboration as well as for the purpose of contradiction of the evidence of the maker only. Let us now see whether the F.I.R. which is the earlier version of the prosecution case could be taken up for consideration to find out the inconsistencies of the statements made therein with the evidence led during trial. It is true that F.I.R. cannot be used to contradict any witness other than the informant, but the Court can take notice of the earliest recorded statements with regard to the prosecution case in the context of the circumstances particularly when the informant is not available for deposing in the Court because of her death and when the P.W. 1 and P.W.2 being her companions stated to have seen the assault and thereafter went to the police station and was, present at the time when the F.I.R. was lodged. In such circumstances the Court is entitled to note the conflict between first reported version of the prosecution ease and the story made out in cross-examination in the trial Court. In the case of State Vs. Basirullah reported in 16 D.L.R. page 189 Murshed, J. as he then was held: 

 It is true that a first information report cannot be used to contradict any witness other than the informant; but the Court can and should take notice of the earliest recorded statement with regard to the prosecution case in the context of the circumstances which make this particular report as of vital importance in the assessment of prosecution evidence. 

 9. In their evidence P.W. 1 and P.W.2 who are said to be eye witnesses to the occurrence and actual assault on the victim gave exaggerated version which are quite inconsistent with the statements made in the F.I.R. and the external injuries found by the doctor on the body of the deceased. And such basic inconsistencies amounting 10 false fines, cannot be ignored for weighing the value of the evidence of P.Ws. This view is supported by the view taken in the case of Taleb @ Talebor Vs. State reported in P.L.D. 1967(SC) 17: 

 10. It is true that the statement made in the F.I.R. does not bind the other persons as it only contradicts and corroborates the maker, but there may be circumstances where the F.I.R. can be taken into consideration to see the subsequent developments and inconsistencies of the prosecution cases and departure made from the initial statements. In the present case, though F.LR. was lodged by Halima Khatun (now deceased), she was not alone in the police station while lodging the F.I.R. P.W.1 being her son, P.W.2 being second wife of her husband also went to the police station as it appears from the evidence. In the case of Liakat Ali Chaklader and 3 others Vs. The State reported in B.C.R. 1984 (AD) 114, it is observed as follows:— 

 12. Referring to the law laid down in the case cited above and in the series of judicial pronouncements, we now propose to proceed to assess the value of the evidence of the P.Ws. just opposition with the statements made in the F.I.R. and the deposition of P.W. 1 and 2 in our quest, we find the following points worth mentioning: 

 (1) In the F.I.R. it is stated that the P.W. 1 Atiar along with his father deceased Akbar Sheik went out together from the house to the bank of the canal near the dingi boat. P.W. 1 in his evidence stated that his father already left the house and started for catching fish while he himself being still in the house went to his mother to bring rice and at that time, on hearing hue and cry of 5/6 persons from outside, he ran towards the place. 

 (2) In the F.I.R. it is stated that the victim was taken to the house of Kanai Kazi and was mercilessly beaten there, but during evidence P.W. 1 said that the victim was taken to the house of Mannan Kazi and was beaten there. 

 (3) In his evidence P.W.J stated that the victim Akbar Sheik was beaten in the house of Mannan Kazi and his necl was broken being hard pressed; Mannan Kazi gave order for breaking his legs, Khokon kazi brought Sabol, Razzaque Kazi broke the legs, Babul Kazi ordered Bachchu Kazi to finish Akbar Sheik and thereafter the injured was taken to the house of Chairman Mohiuddin and thereafter his brother Ahiya came to the place. This statements do not find mentioned in the F.I.R. 

 (6) In the F.I.R. the story of beating was not mentioned as the motive for the assault on the victim Akbar Sheik but in evidence there is a remarkable departure on this material point. 

 13. We have already discussed the evidence of P.W.1 and 2. Let us now take-up for discussion the evidence of P.W.15 Mohiuddin Sheik, son of Saikh Aminuddin who is said to be present at the place of occurrence and has seen the accused appellant's assaulting deceased Akbar Sheik. P.W. 15 is a landless labourer who used to work earlier in the house of Ahiya, the brother of the Chairman. He has given a vivid picture of the tragic epso deposing himself as an eye-witness though as a matter of fact he could not be treated as such but the learned trial Court has placed much reliance on the oral evidence of the witness who, according to the trial court, is an independent eyewitness of the occurrence. The evidence of the said witness is that at the relevant time he heard hue and cry on his way back from the heel and the children of Kazi Family then told him that Nazim Kazi, Aftab Kazi, Khokon Kazi, Aslam, Shahid Kazi caught hold of deceased Akbar Sheik. He said, on getting this information he went near the shop of the Shahid Kazi and saw the accused Aftab Kazi was assaulting the deceased with Kocha blows. He also stated that accused Mannan Kazi reached there by a rickshaw and assaulted the deceased with kicks after passing an order and thereby breaking his legs and hands. He said, on such order by the accused Mannan Kazi, accused Khokon Kazi brought a Sabol and handed it to Razzaque Kazi and a brick was put under the legs of Akbar and caused damage to the legs of the deceased with the help of Shahid. He said that thereafter he went towards the house of the Chairman, Khokon Kazi, Aftab Kazi, Nazim Kazi Mannan Kazi and carried the victim in a gunny bag and left him in front of the house of the Chairman. He also said, immediately thereafter, Chairman came there by a motor cycle and the victim uttered something in feeble voice. The learned trial court found that this witness was neither a relation of the deceased nor had any enmity with the accused persons and as such there was nothing to disbelieve his evidence. While placing reliance on the evidence of P.W.15, the learned trial court has ignored certain important aspect which has rendered the evidence of P.W. 15 unreliable and hence unacceptable. As a matter of fact the witness made his maiden appearance as a witness in the court during trial for the first time. Before that the other witnesses. particularly the Witness No.1 and 24 who are also said to be eyewitnesses, did not even know that P.W. 15 was an eye-witness. The name of the P.W. was neither mentioned in the FIR. nor in the charge-sheet as a witness. P.W.16, the I.O., in reply to the cross-examination, admitted that he did not interrogate the witness Mohiuddin, son of Afiluddin, though, as Police Officers, they always interrogate the persons from whom the clue to the crime may be available. He also admitted that he has not recorded the statement of the witness Mohiuddin taken under section 161 of the Cr. P.C. 

 14. P.W. 1 Atiar Rahman, P.W. 2 Asia Khatun, while giving description of the occurrence and stating the names of the persons present at the place of occurrence, did not utter the name of the witness Mohiuddin as being seen at the place of occurrence even at a fairly distant place. At the same time, the evidence of P.W. 15 does not show that he disclosed that he saw the occurrence. The witness also does not say that P.W. 1 and P.W.2 and or other witnesses except P.W. 11 were seen by him. So, if the evidence of P.W. 1, 2 and IS is considered together, the evidence of P.W. 1 and 2 exclude the possibility of P.W.15 being present at the place and at the time of occurrence and in the same way the evidence of P.W. 15 excludes the possibility of the presence of P.W. 1 and 2 as having seen the occurrence and assault on the deceased by the accused appellants. From the above facts appearing on the face of the evidence of P.W.1, 2 and P.W.16, the I.O., it becomes very difficult for us to believe that the P.W. 15 Mohiuddin Sheik was present at the time and place where the occurrence alleged to have taken place and, therefore, no reliance can be placed on his evidence. For the above reasons, the evidence of P.W.15 is taken out of consideration and the evidence of P.Ws. 1 and 2 also remains questionable. Thus, we find it unsafe to place any credence on the evidence of aforesaid 3 P.Ws. so far it relates to the manner of occurrence and the involvement of accused appellants with it. We now intend to proceed with the discussion of the evidence of other prosecution witnesses. 

 15. P.W. Hasan Ali Sheik stated in his evidence that Akbar Sheik died on 24th Aswin, 1983, Sheik was taken to the house of Kanai Kazi and then to the house of Mannan Kazi. He said that he came and had talk with Akbar but found that he could not talk properly. He called rikshaw and his brother Kashem and Salam took the victim towards the hospital. He himself, the Chairman, Giasuddin Haider and Sarif Halder also went to the police station. The witness was declared hostile and cross-examined by the prosecution. In reply to cross-examination, this witness mentioned the names of Aftab Kazi, Mannan Kazi, Babul Kazi as being present there. He denied to have seen the accused beating Akbar Sheik. He admitted the defence suggestion that Akbar committed theft and he was beaten on many occasions by the villagers. He denied the prosecution suggestion that the Chairman asked him not to depose against the accused. This witness has not said anything about the presence of P.W.1 and 2 and 15 at the place of occurrence. The positive answer given by this witness is that he has not seen the accused persons beating the victim and this has dealt a fatal blow to the prosecution case. P.W.4 Nur Ahmed Sheik said only about the death of Akbar Sheik. He was cross-examined by the prosecution, on being declared hostile. He also denied to have seen the accused persons assaulting Akbar Sheik, but admitted that the Chairman is the relation of accused appellants. 

 19. P.W.8 Hasem Sheik stated that he came to know from the shop keeper Abdul that some unknown persons killed Akbar and left him before his house. Ongoing near the place, he found the victim in injured condition with hands and legs damaged. He said that the deceased was stating some something in a very feeble voice. We will discuss about the evidence of this witness further while we will take up and deal with the matter relating to the dying declaration later on. 

 22. P.W.11 Mohiuddin Abmed son of Late Sheik Moizuddin Ahmed was the then Chairman of the local Union Parishad. He says that on the day of occurrence while returning home from outside after evening, he heard a hue and cry on the road in front of his house. On query be came to know that Akbar was left in a serious injured condition in a gunny bag with his legs and hands damaged and eyes extracted. On being asked by him the victim gave the names of the accused Nazim Kazi, Babul Kazi, Mannan Kazi, Aftab Kazi and Amjad Kazi as his assailants in feeble voice. He said that on the following day daroga visited the place of occurrence, seized some alamats, such as rod, sabol etc. He, however denied the defence suggestion that P.W. 15 Mohiuddin Kazi did not tell him the names of Nazim Kazi, Aftab Kazi, Mannan Kazi, Amjad Kazi to him in feeble voice. From the evidence, it appears that he is not an eye witness to the occurrence, but he claimed that before him, the victim Akbar Sheik made statements disclosing the names of the accused before his death. The value and importance of the so-called dying declaration will be dealt with at a subsequent stage. 

 27. Let us pause for a moment and evaluate the evidence of Doctor placing it side by side with the evidence of the P.Ws. 1 and 2. From the evidence of the witnesses, it transpires that the bones of legs and hands were smashed and the eye of the victim was extracted, but the report of the Doctor do not give any indication of such injuries, rather the Doctor has found some injuries which could only be caused by sharp cutting weapons which is not borne out from the evidence of witnesses who did not say that any such sharp cutting weapon was used for causing injury on the body of the deceased Akbar Sheik. The nature of the injuries which are said to have been inflicted on the body of Akbar Sheik as stated by the prosecution witnesses and the injuries found by the Doctor on the body of the deceased while holding autopsy are quite different. 

 28. Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, while drawing our attention to the evidence of P.W. 1 and 2 submitted that the so-called eye witnesses have given an exaggerated account of injury which is quite inconsistent with the marks of injuries found by the Doctor on the body of the deceased and this conflict with regard to injuries arising out of the evidence of P.Ws. 1 and 2 and that of the Doctor falsify the occular evidence which cannot be reconciled in determining the guilt of the accused appellants. The learned Advocate referred to the case of Taleb @ Talebor and others Vs. The State reported in 1967 P.L.D. (SC) P-16, wherein also the evidence of the eye-witnesses giving an account of the injuries caused on the deceased was found exaggerated as it was inconsistent with the medical report and, accordingly, it was held: 

 "It was not in accordance with recognized principles applicable to the appreciation of such evidence to ignore the basic falsities that appear and to accept only a part of the statement of one witness, itself made in cross-examination and constituting a major departure from the account given of the whole occurrence by the same witness for the purpose of holding a part of the charges proved against only one or two of a large number of accused persons. On the state of the evidence, it could not be said with any confidence, that the two injuries of the deceased were not the result of latihi blows delivered by the alleged assailants other than the resent appellants, that is a sufficient basis for giving the appellants the benefit of a patent doubt appearing on the face of the evidence in respect of the charge of having caused the death of the deceased persons." 

 "The direct testimony in the case of the statements of Fazal Dad, Mansabdar and Ajaib who claimed to be eye-witness as they are very closely connected with the deceased as also interse. In view of their animosity with he accused party which was not denied, their statements required a careful scrutiny. The learned trial Judge found that the statements suffered from grave discrepancies on account of the effect of the witnesses to fit in their statements with the medical evidence about the injuries sustained by P.Ws. Mansabdar and Ajaib. It was also held that the total grief suffered by the complainant party was incommensurate with the number of the alleged assailants and the possibility of false Implication of Innocent persons very much existed in the case." 

 30. In the present ease, P.W.1 has gone to the extent of saying that the legs of the deceased Akbar Sheik was fractured and damaged and the eye was extracted. P.W.2 also similarly says in her evidence that the legs of the deceased Akbar Sheik was fractured due to shabol blows by accused appellants Amjad Sheik. The account of these injunes given by the witnesses being highly exaggerated, comes in direct conflict with the expert's opinion and evidence of the Doctor P.W. 14. In view of such highly exaggerated account of the injuries and inconsistency in the evidence of the P.W.1 and 2, we do not consider it proper to place reliance on such tainted occular evidence of the interested witnesses. The prosecution has banked upon the statements alleged to have been made by the deceased Akbar Sheik, who was said to have disclosed before his death the names of the accused appellants as assailants as the last swan song. 

 31. Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused appellants submits that the statements alleged to have been made by the deceased, mentioning the names of the accused appellants, not only lacks the gravity of the dying declaration but it also becomes doubtful as to whether such statements were at all made by the deceased before P W 7, P W 8 and P W 11. In this respect the learned Advocate referring to the evidence of P.Ws. 1 and 2, submits that these witnesses who are said, to be present at the place of occurrence have not stated anything about such statements being made before the P.W. 7, P.W.8 and P.W.11. The F.I.R. also is conspicuously silent about the making of such dying declaration before the said witnesses. 

 "A dying declaration is relevant and material evidence in the prosecution of the assailants and a truthful and reliable dying declaration may form the sole basis of conviction, even though it is not corroborated. But the Court must be satisfied that die declaration is truthful. The reliability of the declaration should be subjected to a close scrutiny, considering that it was made in the absence of the accused who had no opportunity to test its veracity by cross- examination, if the Court finds that the declaration is not wholly reliable and a material and integral portion of the deceased's version of the entire occurrence, the Courts may in all the circumstances of the case, consider it unsafe to convict the accused on the basis of the declaration alone without further corroboration. It was held on facts that considering all the circumstances of the case, the dying declaration suffered from an infinity and were not reliable by the themselves and could not safely form the basis of the conviction of the accused without further corroboration. As no such corroboration was forthcoming in the case, the accused were given the benefit of doubt and were acquitted." 

 In the present case the dying declaration is stated to have been made orally before the P.W.11. The local Chairman and 1.W.7 disclosing the names of the appellants as assailants, no it depends upon the oral testimony of the witnesses before whom it is alleged to have been made and, therefore, it does not stand on the same footing with those statements which are found to have been made before independent and reliable persons and if it is reduced to writing. As the dying declaration, in the present case, is said to be made before the persons whose character and position in relation to the accused persons is not above board and it suffers from inherent infirmities. Furthermore, we have already found that the fact relating to the discloser of the names of the appellants before P.W. 11 and P.W.7 was not brought to light earlier while the F.I.R was lodged though P.W. 11 was found to have gone to the police station along with the informant. Again, from the evidence given and during cross-examination, P.W.7 and P.W. 11 and the I.O. P.W. 16, it is found that the witnesses themselves did not mention before the I.O. anything about the dying declaration while their statements were recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 36. Thus, we find that the alleged dying declaration of the deceased suffers from inherent weakness and infirmities as a piece of evidence so as to inspire us to place any reliance on it. Furthermore, this vital point was not brought to the knowledge of the accused appellants while they were examined under section 342 if the Code of Criminal Procedure. Therefore, we are of the view that it will be quite unsafe to uphold the conviction of the accused appellants relying on the dying declaration without corroboration. From the evidence adduced, it appears that the prosecution had been able to prove the case of death of Akbar Sheik. The defence denied the way and manner of ordinance and involvement of the accused persons. From the side of the defence it was suggested that Akbar Sheik was a man of questionable character and might have been taken to task without any intention to kill by the angry villagers because of the conduct. Further, the defence Suggestion put to the P.Ws. 3 and 4 was that on the date he was caught while committing theft in the house of Mahbub Kazi and Mannan Kazi and the said P.Ws., though denied the particular occurrence suggested by the defence, admitted that the deceased Akbar Sheik was a man of bad habit of stealing and for that he was beaten on many occasions. The admission of the prosecution witnesses goes in favour of the defence version of the case. The defence case gets further support from the deposition of the I.O. while he stated that Mabbub Kazi was arrested by him and then let off Curiously enough, the said Mahbub kazi is not here a witness nor and accused in this case. The learned Advocate for the appellants has, then drawn our attention to the contradictory evidence of the witnesses with reference to the statements made under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the I.O. From the inconsistencies between the statements made in the F.I.R., the statements made under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the subsequent deposition of the witnesses recorded in the Court, we find that there is remarkable departure from the starting point of the prosecution case and the subsequent stages with the introduction of some new development which was not in the F.I.R. and also in the statements made under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal procedure. In this case we find that besides the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2, who are close relations and P.W. 16 who kept himself invisible so long before the trial started, there is no other eye-witness. The other witnesses said to have been present on the date, time, and place of occurrence did not say anything about the presence and participation of the accused appellants in the commission of the offence. In this connection our attention has been drawn to the point that the P.Ws. also mentioned the presence of many other persons at the time and place of occurrence but they have neither been examined nor even cited as witness in this case. Non examination of those persons and the neighbours as witnesses also has rendered the prosecution case doubtful and entitling the defence to the benefit under Section 114(G) of the Evidence Act. The learned Advocate for the appellants submits from the facts and circumstances and the evidence on record, we are of the view that the prosecution suffers from serious infirmity. We find that the prosecution has failed to prove the case against the appellants beyond all reasonable doubt and in that view of the matter the judgment and order of conviction and, sentence passed by the learned trial Court cannot be sustained.
